prompt:
Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: handmade layered paper sculpture (紙雕 / kirie), the same for buildings, trees, plants,
fences and props. Every shape is a piece of cut paper: visible paper fibres, slightly soft
hand-cut edges, pieces overlapping in shallow layers with small soft contact shadows where one
sheet sits on another. Colour is printed on the paper: clearly visible risograph / stencil print
grain and uneven ink density across every flat area, never a clean digital fill.
Details are built from small cut pieces (roof tiles, bricks, window frames, leaves, petals,
wood planks), not painted lines.
Colour: follow the real object, then mute it: pale, slightly greyed, warm. Typical tones: warm
cream, pale brick red, coral, sage and grey-green, mustard, indigo, wood brown, stone grey.
No saturated red-against-green contrast.
Do NOT make: a 3D render or clay/plastic model, smooth bevelled relief, realistic or painterly
illustration, photo textures, thick foam layers, glow, glossy highlights, black outline strokes,
smooth gradients, depth of field.
Output: generated natively on a fully TRANSPARENT background (real alpha, no chroma-key colour
behind it, no coloured fringe), every object complete and separated by clear transparent
gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the object, no text, no captions, no logos.
View: front-facing, very slight three-quarter, the same for every object on the sheet.

Use case: style-transfer. Single sprite. Images 1–3 are the approved style references: Literature Museum (primary), machiya and Shennong street house. Match their muted printed ink, visible paper fibres and finely cut edges. Override general view above with a strictly head-on orthographic elevation: no side, top, or underside planes, no converging lines. Use three or four flat sheets in shallow overlap with only tiny contact shadows. Weathering is a few subtly lighter/darker same-colour paper patches. Keep clean native alpha, generous transparent margins, no halo.
Image 4 is the real gate for architecture and palette; image 5 is the old sprite, for its silhouette and colours only. Redraw the entire Tainan Confucius Temple east gate. Central open rectangular passage is truly transparent, open through to the bottom. Two muted orange-red piers on each side, each drawn as a flat trapezoid widening toward the bottom. Dark purple-brown timber and a blank black plaque with a muted gold frame. Orange tile roof with long upturned swallowtail silhouette, smaller swallowtail on each pier group, and one short low red wall on either side. Assemble roof tiles from repeated flat strips and scalloped snippets, with no cylinders or bevels. Use flat curved cutouts for ridges and small cut-paper accents in muted slate blue, cream and ochre. Match overall silhouette and proportions of reference 5. No letters, scenery, or ground.
Keep the entire gate within the middle 86% of canvas width and height. Outside the silhouette and throughout the open doorway render alpha exactly zero, clear up to every cut edge. No blur whatsoever on the backdrop. Roof tiles are flat stamped scalloped paper shapes with no cylindrical bodies or round projecting ends.
